reason: Findings were source-rechecked by the primary auditor, but no qualified independent reviewer evidence exists.

title: Release evidence workflow can mask three failing producers behind tee
actual: All three authoritative commands run as command | tee in steps marked continue-on-error; the final gate trusts each step outcome. The steps do not explicitly select bash with pipefail or enable it in the script.
impact: A BLOCKED/nonzero release preflight, evidence audit or status command can appear successful, allowing the workflow to report green while uploading incomplete evidence.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: The final gate checks step outcomes, not the left side PIPESTATUS, and upload-artifact only proves files exist.
minimal_fix: Set shell: bash and set -euo pipefail for each step, or capture producer output/exit code explicitly before upload; add a test that forces each producer nonzero.
evidence_to_close: workflow test proving each producer nonzero makes the job fail
rollback: Revert the workflow-only patch if artifact upload or shell compatibility regresses.

title: Remote governance workflow can swallow the audit wrapper BLOCKED exit
actual: The remote-audit command is piped to tee in a run step without explicit pipefail.
impact: Missing branch protection, required checks/reviews or authentication can return nonzero from the wrapper while tee returns zero, making the evidence workflow misleadingly successful.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: if-no-files-found:error checks only artifact presence; a BLOCKED JSON file can still be uploaded from a green job.
minimal_fix: Run the step with explicit bash/pipefail or preserve and re-emit the producer exit code after tee; add a forced-BLOCKED workflow test.
evidence_to_close: remote wrapper nonzero propagates through tee
rollback: Revert the workflow shell change if the runner shell proves incompatible.

title: PASS-time checkpoint does not enforce task Expected New Paths or Forbidden Touches
actual: Expected New Paths are parsed for stale-resume dirty allowlisting. checkpoint() collects and stages the post-run worktree without comparing paths to the task manifest and does not parse Forbidden Touches.
impact: A task can reach a checkpoint containing out-of-scope changes if verify prose fails to catch them; task PASS evidence then overstates scope integrity.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: git diff --check validates whitespace only, and the initial clean-worktree check does not constrain changes created during the task.
minimal_fix: Parse both allow/deny sections into a canonical manifest and reject unexpected staged paths before commit; test additions, modifications, deletions, renames and generated evidence exceptions.
evidence_to_close: task-scoped PASS log and independent review
rollback: Keep the prior checkpoint path behind a temporary compatibility switch only during test rollout; never auto-commit on validation failure.

title: Retained v1 mark command can write completed without verify PASS evidence
actual: mark --status completed checks doctor/task/dependencies, then writes progress status/note/time. It does not require a verify log, VERIFY_RESULT: PASS, summary, checkpoint hash or recovery authorization; --force can bypass dependency checks.
impact: The historical progress ledger can be made to claim completion without reconstructable verification, undermining the no-backfill rule.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Current policy text says mark is progress only, but downstream readers and humans still use progress as evidence; the write path itself has no evidence binding.
minimal_fix: Make the historical tool read-only by default or require a signed/hashed verify evidence bundle plus explicit recovery mode; preserve existing history and never rewrite old runs.
evidence_to_close: negative tests for missing verify evidence
rollback: Restore read-only historical inspection if stricter recovery mode breaks legacy audit use; do not revert historical files.

title: Closed release residuals can accept unbound checksum and incomplete Gatekeeper evidence
actual: formal_dmg.sha256 and formal_release.artifact_dmg_sha256 use only NON_EMPTY validation; no SHA-256 format, same-artifact binding or cross-record equality check exists. spctl status is checked, but required_source=Notarized Developer ID is not validated.
impact: Hand-filled nonempty strings and a generic pass token can close v1-rl-003/v1-rl-004 without proving that the notarized/stapled DMG, checksum, Gatekeeper result and release record all identify the same bytes.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: evidence-audit validates scalar presence/enumeration rather than artifact identity and transcript semantics.
minimal_fix: Validate 64-hex digests, require one artifact identifier across records, recompute/compare checksum in a read-only probe, and parse spctl source/output plus notary submission/staple identifiers.
rollback: Keep stricter validation additive; old pending records remain blocked rather than rewritten.

title: Manual recovery PASS records omit required per-record fields and the test cannot detect it
actual: M-01, M-03 and M-04 are declared pass in prose but omit operator, evidence_paths and the named user_file_invariants as structured fields. The test only searches each field name somewhere in the whole document, so the top-level schema template satisfies it.
impact: A release checklist can cite recovery PASS without a uniquely attributable, path-linked, invariant-complete record; missing evidence may remain invisible to CI.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Global substring assertions do not parse records or associate required fields with each manual_evidence_id/status.
minimal_fix: Move records to parseable structured blocks/files, validate each pass record against a schema, and require evidence paths plus invariant results; keep local QA scope explicit.
evidence_to_close: per-record schema tests with negative fixtures
rollback: Leave current prose as historical context while introducing additive structured records; do not rewrite the claimed run data.

title: Release dispatch input labels artifacts but does not select the audited release
actual: inputs.release is used only in the artifact name; all commands receive no release argument and release_status.py hard-codes v0.1.0.
impact: An operator can request another release string and receive an artifact named for it even though the contents audit v0.1.0, weakening traceability.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Artifact naming is not content binding, and current status output does not echo/validate the dispatch input.
minimal_fix: Either remove the input and use a fixed artifact name, or pass a validated release identifier through every command and record it inside each JSON payload.
rollback: Return to fixed v0.1.0 naming if multi-release selection is not supported.

title: Remote governance workflow reads an undeclared branch input
actual: workflow_dispatch declares no inputs, but the branch-selection step reads github.event.inputs.branch; manual dispatch therefore cannot provide that value and the audit falls back to the repository default branch.
impact: Operators cannot intentionally audit another protected branch even though the script suggests that capability; evidence may be attributed to the wrong branch.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: The fallback produces a valid branch and does not fail, so structural workflow checks can miss the misconfiguration.
minimal_fix: Declare and validate a branch input, or delete the dead branch-input path and explicitly document/default the protected branch.
evidence_to_close: JSON records selected and resolved branch
rollback: Remove optional branch selection if branch-specific operation is not needed.

title: RISK_POLICY=allow conflicts with the repository's Mission-Critical confirmation rule
actual: The runtime says allow injects authorization and stops waiting even for High/Mission-Critical tasks, while adjacent rules say those boundaries still require explicit confirmation and cannot be bypassed.
impact: An environment-wide flag may be treated as task-specific consent for user-file/DB/iCloud/privacy actions, creating ambiguous authorization evidence.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Static wording checks can validate both sentences independently but do not resolve their precedence or bind consent to a specific task.
minimal_fix: Define one authority rule: require a task-scoped approval record for Mission-Critical actions, with allow limited to already approved queues and explicit path/risk scope.
rollback: Default to pause when approval metadata is missing or ambiguous.

title: DMG Gatekeeper assessment command differs between source guide and evidence tooling
actual: The guide requires spctl --type open for DMG, while the evidence template/tool use --type install.
impact: Future evidence can be collected under two incompatible command semantics and still be labeled the same gate.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Current records are pending, so scalar status checks do not compare command provenance.
minimal_fix: Choose the documented macOS assessment mode, centralize it in one source, and record full command/tool version/output in evidence.
evidence_to_close: command compatibility test on a notarized DMG
rollback: Retain both commands as explicitly distinct checks if both are required; never silently rename old evidence.

title: Release checklist records remote CI success without a reproducible run identity
actual: The checklist cites a date, commit prefix and three workflow names as completed/success, but provides no run IDs, URLs or machine-readable snapshot.
impact: The historical claim cannot be independently reproduced or used as fresh remote merge/release evidence.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Local docs/tests can confirm the sentence exists but cannot query or authenticate the claimed remote state.
minimal_fix: Store wrapper JSON containing repository, branch, commit, run IDs/URLs, timestamps and protection snapshot; refresh it for the release candidate.
rollback: Keep the prose as historical context but mark it non-current until machine evidence exists.

title: Tracked 94 MB universal static archive lacks source/tool fingerprint and consumer binding
actual: Git tracks a universal x86_64/arm64 Mach-O archive (blob 093146967775a8de08ecca00e2c65dfbfe3b2b2f). The documented build output is ignored Bridge/Generated, and the Xcode project search shows tracked UniFFI headers/Swift bindings but no explicit reference to this archive.
impact: The repository carries opaque executable bytes whose generating source/toolchain and actual release consumption are not proven; stale or substituted bytes are difficult to detect.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: A Git blob hash proves identity only, not reproducibility, source binding or that the build consumes it.
minimal_fix: Remove the stale archive if unused, or replace it with a reproducible artifact manifest containing source commit/tool versions/fingerprint and an explicit verified consumer path.
rollback: If removal breaks a hidden consumer, restore the exact Git blob while adding explicit project linkage and provenance tests.

title: CI installs mutable Rust/coverage/Swift lint tool selections
actual: Rust uses stable, cargo-llvm-cov is installed without a package version, and Homebrew installs the current SwiftLint/SwiftFormat formulas.
impact: The same commit can receive different formatting, lint or coverage results as tool releases move; no current bypass was demonstrated.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: Configuration files pin rules but not executable versions; --locked pins cargo-llvm-cov dependencies, not the selected package release.
minimal_fix: Record/pin compatible tool versions in a checked-in toolchain/CI manifest and expose versions in job output; update via reviewed dependency changes.
rollback: Revert an incompatible pin while retaining the last known-good version record.

title: Documented post-release observation has no structured closure fields
actual: The guide requires download/install checks and monitoring of crashes, import failures, DB consistency, iCloud and AI provider errors with owner/SLO, but v1-rl-003/v1-rl-004 closure requirements contain none of those fields.
impact: After a future release, the repository cannot mechanically prove the observation window or escalation/rollback decision occurred.
why_existing_checks_insufficient: release status stops at pre-release distribution/tag fields.
minimal_fix: Add a post-release observation record with window, data sources, owner/SLO, incidents and promote/rollback decision, without blocking pre-tag gates that cannot yet observe production.
rollback: Keep the record optional until a formal release exists, then gate release closeout rather than tag creation.
